claims.text: Language model performance improves with increasing model scale.
Language model calibration improves with increasing model scale.
Language model performance and calibration across BIG-bench tasks are poor in absolute terms.
Language model performance and calibration are poor when compared with human expert rater performance.
Performance across different model classes is remarkably similar, with sparse architectures providing additional benefits.
Tasks that show gradual and predictable performance improvements commonly involve a large knowledge or memorization component.
Tasks that exhibit breakthrough behavior at a critical scale often involve multiple steps, multiple components, or brittle metrics.
Social bias in language models typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context.
Prompting can improve or mitigate the scale-dependent increase in social bias in ambiguous contexts.

evidence.description: Evaluations of OpenAI GPT models, Google dense transformers, and Switch transformers across scale parameters show performance improves with scale.
Evaluation across scaling tiers demonstrates calibration gains alongside scale increases on BIG-bench tasks.
Across 204 BIG-bench tasks, models demonstrated low overall performance and calibration in absolute terms.
Human expert raters completed all tasks to establish a baseline, significantly outperforming all evaluated model scale tiers.
Comparison between OpenAI GPT, Google-internal dense transformers, and Switch-style sparse transformers showed similar trajectories with sparse benefits.
Analysis of task performance curves revealed that tasks relying heavily on memorization or knowledge showed linear/predictable scaling.
Analysis showed tasks exhibiting non-linear performance jumps at critical scale thresholds were characterized by multi-step reasoning, composite sub-tasks, or brittle evaluation metrics.
Evaluations on social bias tasks demonstrated higher measured bias at larger model parameters when context was ambiguous.
Experiments with task prompting demonstrated reductions in measured social bias growth at higher scale limits.

methodologies.name: BIG-bench Evaluation Framework
methodologies.description: Extensive empirical benchmarking across 204 diverse tasks evaluating OpenAI GPT, Google dense transformers, and Switch-style sparse transformers from millions to hundreds of billions of parameters, alongside human expert baselines.
conditions: Model scale spanning millions to hundreds of billions of parameters
Prompting interventions on social bias tasks

limitations.text: Model performance and calibration on BIG-bench remain poor in absolute terms and fall far short of human expert raters.
Social bias in language models increases as model scale grows when evaluating in ambiguous context settings.
